subject: Hosted API availability: brief impact notice and next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Russo <alex.russo@sablehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API availability: brief impact notice and next steps

Alex / SableHealth ops team,

Quick note to let you know we’ve observed elevated partial responses and truncated streaming for a segment of requests in our hosted US-EAST pool (affecting ~3-6% of token streaming flows) since ~08:50 PT. We’ve opened an incident (INC-20260523-07) and the on-call and core serving teams are investigating.

What we know so far:
- Symptom: intermittent truncated streams and occasional 5xx on completion for long generation jobs (>1200 tokens).
- Scope: roughly 3–6% of requests routed to US-EAST; customers with high median sequence lengths show higher incidence.
- Impact: degraded completion fidelity and a small rate of failed completions.

What we’re doing now:
- Active mitigation: routing a fraction of affected traffic to alternate model variant pools and temporarily increasing KV cache retention for longer sequences.
- Monitoring: additional p95/p99 telemetry deployed to the customer dashboard & status page.
- Next update: we’ll follow up with a technical summary in ~2 hours or sooner if we have a resolution.

If this is causing visible user-facing failures for you, reply with an example request ID (or attach a short request/response dump) and we’ll prioritize.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you posted.

Sincerely,
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai

--

- Impact: ~10% of our clinical-summary generation jobs are returning truncated outputs; retries lead to higher latency.
- Example request id: req_9f3b2a7c (attached minimal payload and received output).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosted API availability: brief impact notice and next steps

Alex — thanks for the example request id and payload. We dug into the traces and logs for req_9f3b2a7c. Short summary of findings so far: 

- Root symptom (early): unexpectedly large attention-window and long continuation tokens triggered aggressive prefetch paths in our multipath fanout. That produced transient KV-cache evictions under concurrent pressure which led to partial trailing-outputs when the server had to re-assemble kv-state mid-stream.

- Immediate mitigation applied (11:10 PT):
  * Enabled temporary soft-throttles on prefetch fanout for US-EAST.
  * Pinned a small percentage of traffic to an alternate model pool with higher KV retention.
  * Increased request-level retry window to allow a clean full re-try rather than returning partial.

- Client-side workarounds you can consider while we complete the fix:
  1) Set max_tokens to <=1100 for streaming jobs that can tolerate shorter answers.
  2) If you have a short timeout in your client, extend streaming timeout by +2s to allow retries to complete.
  3) Optionally route critical calls to our EU pool (region=eu) — we can enable a cross-region pin for your tenant (we can do this for a short window).

- ETA: we expect the full fix (KV lifecycle adjustment + prefetch backpressure tuning) to be rolled to US-EAST in the next 4–6 hours, barring regressions. We’ll update the status page and share a follow-up postmortem.

I’ll attach the sample logs we pulled and keep you posted. If you prefer a quick call to walk through the workaround, I’m available at 12:30 PT.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Hosted API availability: brief impact notice and next steps — incident resolved

Alex — quick resolution summary and next steps (INC-20260523-07):

Status: Resolved at 15:22 PT. All US-EAST serving pools returned to normal completion behavior.

Root cause (high level): An interaction between our prefetch multipath logic and long-sequence workloads produced transient KV-cache churn under a narrow concurrency pattern. When that churn coincided with mid-stream re-assembly we occasionally returned truncated outputs instead of cleanly failing and letting the retry path succeed.

What we changed (short term fixes applied):
- Backpressure applied to prefetch fanout to avoid concurrent kv-eviction cycles.
- Increased per-request KV retention thresholds for affected model variants.
- Improved detection so that if a continuation sequence re-assembly enters an inconsistent state we fail-safe to a retry path instead of returning partial content.

Planned follow-ups (longer term):
- Kernel-level perf tuning to reduce prefetch cost and a controlled rollout of improved KV lifecycles (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Dashboard: we’ll add a p99 "continuation-truncation" metric and an alert tied to customer-facing SLAs.
- Postmortem doc: full timeline, RCA, and mitigations: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/INC-20260523+postmortem (we attached a short incident_summary PDF).

Apologies for the disruption and thank you for the quick examples — they helped narrow the window. If you’d like a call to review the postmortem or to enable a temporary EU pinning for your tenant, let us know and we’ll schedule.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
